what: Rambus licenses chip technology and sells memory interface chips: the buffers and controllers that sit between a processor and its memory, used in data centre servers.
customers: Memory makers and chip designers paying licence fees, and server manufacturers buying its chips.
money: memory interface and companion chips for server modules
licences on memory and security technology patents
moat: Patents on memory interface standards that the whole industry uses, combined with chips designed to those same standards, which gives it both a royalty stream and a product business.
risks: Royalty revenue depends on patent licence renewals, which are negotiated periodically
Only seven analysts cover the stock
opportunities: A 32.6% net margin and $313M of free cash flow on $796M of revenue
Revenue grew from $328M to $708M in four years
Analysts see about 85% upside, and AI servers use far more memory modules per machine, each needing its chips
watch: Product revenue growth tied to server memory shipments.
